detail: 12 independent Toulouse mill companies merge into the Honor del Bazacle with 80 uchaux; the merger charter values the shares (first price, ~531 kg silver for the whole firm).
Two remaining independent mills bought for 16 new uchaux (88 by 1374, 96 by 1384).
First Voyage (GBP68,373) of the EIC, chartered 31 Dec 1600; separate voyage stocks until 1612.
VOC subscription closes (f6,424,588); secondary trading in Amsterdam from Sept 1602 (114%).
EIC First Joint Stock GBP418,691 (terminable, 1613-1616).
EIC Second Joint Stock subscribed GBP1,629,040 (954 subscribers), called in 8 instalments.
WIC (chartered 3 Jun 1621) completes its capital, f7,108,161.
EIC Third Joint Stock GBP420,700.
EIC New General Stock: permanent joint stock, GBP739,782 subscribed, 50% called.
Hudson's Bay Company chartered, capital GBP10,500.
Royal African Company formed, capital GBP111,100.

Insolvent first WIC replaced by a new chartered WIC. Old shareholders got new stock worth 15% of old nominal (after paying 4%), pre-1656 creditors 30%, later creditors 100%; new nominal capital f6,332,362 (no market value at the deal; old shares had fallen to ~15% by 1649-50).
100% stock bonus doubles EIC stock from GBP369,891 to GBP739,782 (price ~460 old basis -> ~150-260 new).
HBC stock trebled by bonus, GBP10,500 -> GBP31,500.
Bank of England incorporated (charter 27 Jul 1694), capital GBP1,200,000.
English (New) East India Company chartered on the GBP2m loan; its stock GBP1,662,000.
Union of the Old and English companies as the United Company, capital GBP3,163,000 (each side GBP1,581,500). Old Company stock at 104.5-105% (GBP1.65m on GBP1.57m) in Feb 1709.
South Sea Company created by converting GBP9.18m of government debt into stock.
RAC reconstruction: old stock written down 90%; total stock GBP451,350.
Compagnie d'Occident founded by John Law; 200,000 shares of 500 L payable in billets d'Etat (issued 1717-18).
Compagnie d'Occident absorbs the East India and China companies and becomes the Compagnie des Indes; new share issues Jun, Jul and Sep-Oct 1719.
Banque Royale merged into the Compagnie des Indes; Company buys the King's 100,000 shares at 9,000 L.
Outstanding 1719 subscriptions converted into shares: 600,000 shares at 12 Mar 1720.
Buy-backs and the King's gift cut shares to 200,000 by 3 Jun 1720; converted 3-for-2 into ~133,000 new shares over the summer.
Royal Exchange Assurance chartered (Bubble Act, 11 Jun 1720 O.S.); traded since 1719 as Onslow's insurance on the Mines Royal shell.
London Assurance chartered (Chetwynd's insurance).
Visa: 125,000 shares presented, reduced to 55,735; ~1,000-1,200 L each in 1722-23 (value ~56-67m L).
Bank of England buys GBP4,000,000 South Sea stock, issuing GBP3,400,000 Bank stock at 118; Bank capital rises to GBP8,959,995. SSC capital ~GBP32m after the 1721 readjustment.
Half of South Sea stock turned into South Sea Annuities (company remains a debt holder).
Further conversion leaves South Sea trading stock at GBP3,662,784, unchanged to 1817+.
Royal African Company dissolved; forts to the Company of Merchants Trading to Africa.
Compagnie des Indes trade monopoly suspended; company winds down (joint-stock companies banned 24 Aug 1793).
First Bank of the United States subscription, $10m.
Second WIC charter not renewed; company and possessions taken over by the States General (shares ~25% of par at the end, GFD chart).
VOC nationalised by the Batavian Republic (last quotes c.120-125% of par = ~f8m); charter lapses 31 Dec 1799.
Million Bank wound up with a surplus paid to stockholders.
Banque de France founded, 30,000 shares x 1,000 F.
First Bank of the United States charter expires; liquidated.
25% stock bonus: capital GBP11,642,400 -> GBP14,553,000.
Second Bank of the United States opens, capital $35m.
Federal charter expired; continued as the Bank of the United States under a Pennsylvania charter, same $35m capital (Dec 1835 value $39.5m)
Final suspension and failure; shares fell to a few dollars (NYSE $1.75 in Dec 1849 during liquidation). Value at end-1835 $39.5m; GFD 1840 $22.9m
North Midland + Midland Counties + Birmingham & Derby Junction railways form the Midland Railway (no values found)
London & Birmingham + Grand Junction + Manchester & Birmingham form the LNWR (no values found for 1846)
South Sea Stock converted under the 1853 debt operations; company wound up (last value seen 1847: c.GBP3.4m)
York Newcastle & Berwick + York & North Midland + Leeds Northern form the North Eastern Railway
Banque de France capital doubled from 91,250 to 182,500 shares (new shares sold at 1,100 fr)
Paris-Lyon and Lyon-Mediterranee merge into the PLM (800,000 shares)
Suez Canal Company subscription closes: 400,000 shares of 500 fr (200m fr)
India Stock (GBP6.0m) redeemed at 200 on 30 Apr 1874 = GBP12.0m; company dissolved 1 Jun 1874
Partial: British government buys the Khedive's 176,602 of 400,000 shares (44%) for GBP3,976,582 = GBP22.52/share, implying GBP9.0m for the whole company
Purchased by the Government of India; shareholders paid in annuities (last company value Dec 1873 GBP29.1m)
Standard Oil Trust agreement: certificates of the trust (c.700,000 initially) replace shares of the constituent companies
Standard Oil Co. (New Jersey) becomes the holding company after the Ohio court dissolved the trust (1892)
Great Indian Peninsula Railway purchased by the Government of India (last value read Dec 1880 GBP26.6m)

J.P. Morgan forms U.S. Steel: $508m common + $510m preferred + $304m bonds; Carnegie Steel bought for ~$480m (mostly in bonds). Market value of the new equity ~$765m (GFD); component market values not found
Royal Dutch/Shell alliance: operating companies owned 60% Royal Dutch, 40% Shell T&T; both parents stay listed
American Tobacco dissolved into American Tobacco, Liggett & Myers, P. Lorillard, R.J. Reynolds (Hannah 1912: AT 169, L&M 58, Lorillard 42 $m)

Supreme Court decree (15 May 1911): 33 subsidiaries distributed pro rata. Sep 1911: NJ ex-subsidiaries 325 + subsidiaries 275 per share (= $590m); Aug 1912 whole worth 1,100/share = $1.08bn. Hannah 1912 values ($m): NJ 390, Indiana 88, NY 73, California 71, Ohio Oil 66*, Prairie 50, Vacuum 26, Atlantic 26
Lancashire & Yorkshire absorbed by LNWR (L&Y last value read Dec 1900 GBP21.6m)
Railways Act 1921 grouping: LNWR (Dec 1920 GBP31.8m) and Midland form the London Midland & Scottish
North Eastern + Great Northern + Great Eastern + others form the LNER (NER Dec 1913 GBP38.8m)
Standard Oil Co. of New York merged with Vacuum Oil to form Socony-Vacuum Oil; socony id continues. No value for Vacuum found.
Bank of England Act 1946: £14.553m Bank Stock exchanged for £58.2m (≈£58m) of 3% Treasury Stock (£400 per £100).
Socony-Vacuum -> Socony Mobil Oil (1955); Mobil Oil (1966); Mobil Corp (1976).
The Texas Company -> Texaco Inc. (1959).
Standard Oil Co. (New Jersey) -> Exxon Corp.

When-issued NYSE trading of "new" AT&T and the 7 regional holding companies begins. Opening prices: old AT&T 62 3/4 (x936.7m sh = $58.8bn); new AT&T 19 ($17.8bn); BellSouth 89 ($8.3bn); Bell Atlantic 65 3/4 ($6.2bn); Ameritech 63 ($5.9bn); Southwestern Bell 62 ($5.8bn); NYNEX 60 1/2 ($5.7bn); US West 56 ($5.2bn); Pacific Telesis 51 1/2 ($4.8bn). Sum of pieces $59.8bn.

AT&T divestiture (Modified Final Judgment). Holders of record 30 Dec 1983 got 1 share of each RHC per 10 AT&T shares. Old AT&T 31 Dec 1983: $57.4bn (936.7m x $61.25, NYSE). Shares of parent value at when-issued close 2 Dec 1983: new AT&T $19.1bn (32%), BellSouth $8.2bn, Bell Atlantic $6.2bn, Ameritech $5.9bn, NYNEX $5.7bn, Southwestern Bell $5.6bn, US West $5.4bn, Pacific Telesis $5.1bn. By 31 Dec 1984 the 8 pieces were worth $73.6bn (AT&T 20.1 + RHCs 53.5).
Texaco acquires Getty Oil (widely reported ~$10.1bn; deal value not re-verified here). Getty end-1983 NYSE value $8.7bn.
Socal acquires Gulf Oil (widely reported ~$13.2bn, then the largest merger ever; not re-verified here). Gulf end-1983 NYSE value $9.1bn. Socal renamed Chevron 1984.
Standard Oil (Indiana) -> Amoco Corp.
Royal Dutch/Shell buys the ~30% public minority of Shell Oil (widely reported ~$5.7bn; not re-verified). Shell Oil end-1984 NYSE value $17.2bn (100%).
GE acquires RCA (widely reported $6.28bn; not re-verified here).
United States Steel -> USX Corp.
NTT listed on Tokyo and 7 other Japanese exchanges; no trade on day 1 (1.28m buy orders), first price ¥1.6m on 10 Feb (15.6m shares -> ¥25.0tn). Government had sold 1.95m shares at ¥1.197m.
KKR leveraged buyout of RJR Nabisco (widely reported ~$25bn incl. debt; not re-verified). RJR end-1988 NYSE equity value $20.9bn.
Bristol-Myers merges with Squibb -> Bristol-Myers Squibb (Squibb value not collected).
AT&T acquires NCR Corporation (stock deal; value not researched; NCR not tracked, spun off again end-1996).
AT&T completes McCaw Cellular purchase (stock); share count rises from 1,352m (end-1993) to 1,569m (end-1994).
Mitsubishi Bank merges with Bank of Tokyo to form Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi (Bank of Tokyo not tracked; deal listed at $33.8bn). Combined value end-1996 (CMC): 88.1bn.
AT&T distributes its remaining 82% of Lucent (IPO of 18% in April 1996). Lucent first CMC value 1997: about 51bn (end-1997). NCR spun off 1996-12-31 (not tracked).
Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz merge to form Novartis (parents not tracked).
Citicorp and Travelers Group merge into Citigroup (Travelers the legal survivor). Citicorp valued at about $70bn in the deal (announced April 1998). Citigroup end-1998: 119.3bn (CMC).
NTT DoCoMo IPO in Tokyo; NTT keeps about 67%. DoCoMo end-1998: 66.5bn; end-1999: 367bn (world #3).
BP merges with Amoco to form BP Amoco (Amoco valued at $48-49bn; not tracked).
Vodafone completes its purchase of AirTouch Communications (value not researched; AirTouch not tracked) and becomes Vodafone AirTouch.
SBC acquires Ameritech (deal $62bn; Ameritech not tracked).
Exxon absorbs Mobil; company renamed Exxon Mobil. Mobil valued at $77.2bn at the December 1998 announcement; Exxon Mobil end-1999 279.9bn (CMC).
Mannesmann board accepts Vodafone AirTouch takeover at EUR 190bn (about $183bn), then the largest takeover ever. Vodafone 31 Mar 2000: 340.3bn (#6 in the world); Mannesmann shares 157.5bn.
Pfizer completes Warner-Lambert takeover (about $90bn; Warner-Lambert not tracked).
Industrial Bank of Japan, Fuji Bank and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank form Mizuho Holdings by share transfer (deal listed at $40.1bn). In 1989 the three were worth JPY 34.2tn together.
AOL and Time Warner complete their merger (announced 2000-01-10: AOL about $163-164bn, Time Warner $83-97bn, deal $162-182bn as variously reported; AOL holders 55%).
Sumitomo Bank and Sakura Bank form Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp (Sakura not tracked; deal listed at $45.5bn); SMFG holding company Dec 2002.
Sanwa Bank and Tokai Bank form UFJ Holdings (Tokai not tracked).

AT&T Corp splits off AT&T Wireless (its tracking stock was 362.75m x $17.31 = 6.3bn at end-2000; the company was sold to Cingular for $41bn in 2004) and Liberty Media (Aug 2001). Children not tracked.
AT&T Broadband spun off and merged into Comcast (deal listed at $72bn); AT&T 1-for-5 reverse split.
Philip Morris Companies renamed Altria Group.
AOL Time Warner renamed Time Warner Inc.
Royal Dutch Petroleum and Shell Transport & Trading unify under Royal Dutch Shell plc (one vessel throughout in this dataset). RDS end-2005: 208.3bn (CAO).
Mitsubishi Tokyo Financial Group absorbs UFJ Holdings (UFJ valued at about $38bn) to form MUFG.
SBC Communications completes purchase of its former parent AT&T Corp for about $16bn and renames itself AT&T Inc. AT&T Corp was worth 157bn in Feb 2000.
ICBC dual IPO in Shanghai and Hong Kong (then the largest IPO). FT end-2006: 254.6bn.
Lucent merges into Alcatel (Alcatel-Lucent). Lucent about 11bn at the end versus 259bn at its Dec 1999 peak.
AT&T Inc. completes the BellSouth acquisition (value not researched; BellSouth not tracked).
Altria spins off Kraft Foods (Kraft had been partly floated in 2001); Kraft value from CMC Mondelez lineage in values.csv.

PetroChina lists A shares in Shanghai; at the A-share close the whole company was briefly valued at about $1tn (peak 1.2tn nominal per Wikipedia), the first "trillion-dollar company" - a paper value since H shares traded far lower.
Altria spins off Philip Morris International. PMI end-2008: 88.0bn (CMC); Altria end-2008: 31.0bn vs 159.3bn end-2007.
Nortel Networks files for bankruptcy protection; peak value 252bn (2000-07-26).
Time Warner spins off Time Warner Cable (not tracked).
Pfizer completes Wyeth acquisition ($68bn; Wyeth not tracked).
Merck completes Schering-Plough merger ($41.1bn; not tracked).
Time Warner spins off AOL Inc. (first CMC value about 2.5bn) - the end of the AOL-Time Warner merger.
ExxonMobil completes XTO Energy acquisition ($41bn; not tracked).
Facebook IPO on Nasdaq.
Alibaba IPO on NYSE (largest IPO until Aramco).
Google reorganises under the new holding company Alphabet Inc. (treated as a rename; Google shares became Alphabet shares one-for-one).
Nokia completes the Alcatel-Lucent takeover (exact completion date not researched).
AT&T Inc. completes its purchase of Time Warner (announced Oct 2016 at $85.4bn equity).
Saudi Aramco IPO on Tadawul (1.5% float, $25.6bn raised); first-day close about $1.88tn, instantly the world #1.
NTT completes its tender for the 34% of DoCoMo it did not own (about $40bn) and delists DoCoMo; DoCoMo was worth about 123bn at end-2020.
Facebook, Inc. renamed Meta Platforms.
AT&T Inc. spins off WarnerMedia, which merges with Discovery to form Warner Bros. Discovery. WBD end-2022: 22.8bn (CMC).
GE spins off 80.1% of GE HealthCare (first CMC values about 26-30bn).
Broadcom completes the VMware acquisition (cash and stock; value not researched; VMware not tracked).
GE spins off GE Vernova; the remaining GE renamed GE Aerospace.
ExxonMobil completes the Pioneer Natural Resources acquisition ($59.5-64.5bn; not tracked).
SpaceX IPO (raised $86bn, the largest IPO ever); peak $2.44tn on 2026-06-19; xAI had been absorbed (about $250bn) in Feb 2026 while private.
